title: Lovable Design Systems: .lovable Folder, Schema, and the File-Copy Model
content:
# Design Systems in Lovable

Design systems in Lovable are **dedicated projects** acting as a single source of truth across a workspace. The design system *is* a Lovable project that other projects connect to — not a config file bolted onto an app.

## The .lovable folder

    .lovable/
    ├── design-system.json          # machine-readable schema
    ├── system.md                   # hand-authored guidelines
    └── rules/
        ├── components.md           # rendered documentation
        ├── design-tokens.md        # token reference
        └── library-guidelines.md   # stack requirements

design-system.json is generated by Lovable; the three rules/*.md files are rendered from it. system.md is the exception and the file practitioners own: it is "preserved across releases, meaning that Lovable does not regenerate it from the schema." It is meant to hold design philosophy and installation context.

## Two component distribution models

**Path A — local source.** Components live in the design system project. Tokens are discovered from "top-level styling files: CSS custom properties in files like src/index.css" or tailwind.config. Components export from src/index.ts or live under src/components/.

**Path B — npm wrapper.** The project wraps an external published package and Lovable reads "the component surface from the package's published type definitions." Private registries need scoped packages with .npmrc auth backed by workspace build secrets:

    @scope:registry=https://your-registry.example.com
    //your-registry.example.com/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}

## Attachment is file copy, not a dependency

When a design system is attached to a project:
- Components copy to src/design-system/<design-system-slug>/
- Knowledge files copy to .lovable/rules/libraries/<design-system-slug>/
- Dependencies merge into package.json
- A [[libraries]] entry in lovable.toml records the connection and version

This is the architecturally distinctive choice: Lovable vendors the design system into each consuming project rather than referencing it. Consequences follow directly — "A project can be connected to at most one design system at a time"; removing a design system severs updates and "copied files become ordinary editable code"; and local edits under src/design-system/ persist only until the next update is accepted, then are clobbered.

## Versioning

Every release bumps a version. Connected projects see an "Update available" prompt in chat. Accepting reruns the file copy against the new version. Draft design systems cannot seed new projects — release first.

## Exclusions

.dsignore controls what does not propagate. Excluded by default: showcase pages (src/pages/, src/routes/, *.stories.ts), test files, and scaffold entrypoints (src/main.tsx, src/App.tsx). Knowledge files in .lovable/rules/*.md always propagate.

## Setup verification

After attachment Lovable runs automatic verification checking "configuration, CSS imports, theme providers, dependencies, and import paths." Notably "verification turns are billed at zero credits" — Lovable does not charge for remediating its own wiring.

## Framework support and gating

"Lovable design systems support React-based component libraries out of the box." Vue, Angular, and Svelte require CSM/FDE consultation. Practitioner reporting indicates the feature is Enterprise-plan gated.

## Reported failure modes

Because attachment is an agent-executed file copy plus dependency merge rather than a deterministic package install, outcomes vary between runs. Practitioners report new projects scaffolding "on a TanStack template even when the design system is a Vite/React one," and the styling framework not always wired into the build automatically — the specific case being "Tailwind 3 pulling in and conflicting with Tailwind 4." This is the concrete cost of the dependency-merge model versus pinned peer dependencies, and explains why the zero-credit verification step exists.
